newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spot Products- Group 3 gasoline rides high.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spot Products- Group 3 gasoline rides high.

text.p: Group Three conventional unleaded gasoline remained the most dynamic product in the lineup of U.S. spot refined products late Thursday, firming solidly amid a spate of refiner buying, players said.

On the futures front, meanwhile, July NYMEX heating oil settled a scant 0.01 cent a gallon higher to 51.45 cents, while July NYMEX gasoline changed direction in the afternoon to settle 0.69 cent lower at 56.09 cents.
MIDCONTINENT
Unleaded gasoline firmed solidly Thursday afternoon in Group Three markets amid a spate of refiner buying, traders said.

Prompt Group unleaded got done at 5.25 cents over July NYMEX, about 0.50 cent firmer than Wednesday. Any July barrels traded at 4.25 cents over the July print, also about half a cent firmer than on Wednesday.
"Unleaded has been the story of the day," said one midcontinent trader, adding it was due to refiners coming out to buy.
One dealer proferred that continuing delays of shipping schedules on the Houston-to-Tulsa-to-Chicago Explorer Pipeline was prompting some refiners to short cover on prompt commitments.
"People are finding themselves short on the prompts and with the Explorer delays people want barrels with a specific date," the player said.

Explorer is about nine days behind schedule and has said barrels for delivery during the early shipment cycle will arrive July 1 or 2. But the broker said market talk is the barrels will not arrive until July 4 or 5.
He also said barrels for late July delivery may not arrive until the first few days of August, while the official Explorer schedule has the barrels arriving end-July.
Differentials were otherwise stable on other Group Three refined products, and in Chicago, which did not see the refiner buying that stoked the Group market, traders said.
NEW YORK HARBOR

Differentials were little changed on all products in the region. NYH prompt "M2" conventional unleaded gasoline was offered at 2.85 cents below July futures, while "A2" reformulated 87-grade held pat with offers at 0.25 cent over, traders said.
"I see no reason to be bullish on gasoline. Crude runs are full-out so we have plenty of gasoline around," one New York player said.
Prompt heating oil remained on offer for about 0.30 cent below July NYMEX, matching the Sun Co posted price listed earlier in the day.
U.S. GULF
Differentials eased slightly on prompt USG heating oil to offers of 2.35 cents below the print, while low sulfur also eased a bit to 1.75 cents under July NYMEX, traders said.
USG prompt conventional unleaded "M1" grade was offered for 3.50 cents below the screen, with diffs holding steady throughout the day.

And USG "V1" 93-octane premium was talked at a 5.75 cent regrade to "M1," little changed from Wednesday diffs despite news Crown Central Petroleum had closed the alkylation unit at its Pasadena, Texas, refinery after a fire early Thursday.
The company said the length of the shutdown had not yet been determined.
